name: STARD 2015
source: Bossuyt PM, Reitsma JB, Bruns DE, Gatsonis CA, Glasziou PP, Irwig L, et al. STARD 2015: an updated list of essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies. BMJ. 2015;351:h5527. https://equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/stard/ | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4623764/

items.text: Identify the report as a diagnostic accuracy study using at least one accuracy metric.
Provide a structured abstract summarizing study design, methods, results, and conclusions.
Explain the scientific and clinical background, including the intended clinical role of the index test.
State the specific diagnostic accuracy objectives and hypotheses.
State whether data collection was planned prospectively before or retrospectively after performing the tests.
Specify participant inclusion and exclusion criteria.
State the basis used to identify potentially eligible participants, such as symptoms or prior test results.
Specify where and when potentially eligible participants were identified, including setting, location, and dates.
State whether enrolled participants formed a consecutive, random, or convenience series.
Describe the index test in sufficient technical detail to allow replication.
Describe the reference standard in sufficient technical detail to allow replication.
Explain the rationale for selecting the reference standard when alternatives exist.
Define and justify index test positivity cut-offs or categories, noting pre-specified versus exploratory thresholds.
Define and justify reference standard positivity cut-offs or categories, noting pre-specified versus exploratory thresholds.
State whether clinical information and reference standard results were available to index test readers.
State whether clinical information and index test results were available to reference standard assessors.
Describe statistical methods used to estimate or compare diagnostic accuracy measures.
Explain how indeterminate index test or reference standard results were handled.
Explain how missing data for the index test and reference standard were handled.
Describe analyses exploring variability in diagnostic accuracy, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory analyses.
Report the target sample size and explain how it was determined.
Present the flow of participants through the study using a diagram.
Report baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of study participants.
Report the distribution of disease severity among participants with the target condition.
Report the distribution of alternative diagnoses among participants without the target condition.
State the time interval and any clinical interventions between index test and reference standard.
Provide a cross-tabulation of index test results against reference standard results.
Report diagnostic accuracy estimates together with their precision, such as 95% confidence intervals.
Report any adverse events resulting from performing the index test or reference standard.
Discuss study limitations, including potential sources of bias, statistical uncertainty, and generalizability.
Discuss clinical practice implications, including the intended use and role of the index test.
Provide the study registration number and name of the registry.
State where the full study protocol can be accessed.
Report funding and support sources and the role of funders in the study.
